interactions.label: Which inflammatory cell is the primary driver of airway damage in COPD, distingu

params.question: Which inflammatory cell is the primary driver of airway damage in COPD, distinguishing its pathogenesis from that of bronchial asthma?

answers.text: Eosinophil

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Eosinophils are the hallmark of asthma's chronic inflammation, not COPD. In COPD, they may appear during some exacerbations but are not the primary drivers of tissue destruction.

answers.text: Mast cell

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Mast cells initiate the early-phase response in asthma through IgE-mediated degranulation. They are not central to COPD pathogenesis.

answers.text: Neutrophil

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. COPD is driven by cigarette smoke activating neutrophils and macrophages, creating a protease–antiprotease imbalance that destroys alveolar walls and causes irreversible obstruction.

answers.text: Basophil

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Basophils play a minor role in allergic responses and are not the primary inflammatory cell in either condition. COPD is characterised by neutrophilic and macrophage-driven inflammation.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the pathophysiology comparison: asthma = eosinophilic inflammation with IgE-mediated mast cell activation; COPD = neutrophilic and macrophage-driven destruction triggered by cigarette smoke.
Well done. Recognising that COPD is neutrophil-driven while asthma is eosinophil-driven is fundamental to understanding why their drug regimens differ.

interactions.label: Why must long-acting beta-2 agonists (LABAs) never be prescribed as monotherapy

params.question: Why must long-acting beta-2 agonists (LABAs) never be prescribed as monotherapy in bronchial asthma?

answers.text: They have no bronchodilator effect when used without an inhaled corticosteroid

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: LABAs are effective bronchodilators on their own. The danger is not lack of efficacy but the masking of worsening eosinophilic inflammation, which leads to fatal exacerbations.

answers.text: They have been linked to increased asthma-related deaths when used without an inhaled corticosteroid

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Clinical evidence showed that LABA monotherapy in asthma increases the risk of fatal and near-fatal exacerbations, because bronchodilation masks ongoing inflammation that continues to worsen unchecked.

answers.text: They cause severe tachycardia that is unique to asthma patients

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Beta-2 agonist cardiac side effects such as tremor and palpitations occur regardless of the underlying disease. The specific mortality risk with LABA monotherapy relates to uncontrolled airway inflammation in asthma.

answers.text: They suppress eosinophil function, worsening the late-phase inflammatory response

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Beta-2 agonists actually inhibit mast cell mediator release rather than worsen eosinophilic inflammation. The danger of monotherapy is symptomatic relief without anti-inflammatory control.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key point: LABAs relieve bronchoconstriction but do not treat the eosinophilic inflammation driving asthma. Used alone, they mask worsening disease and have been linked to increased asthma deaths. In COPD, LABA monotherapy is safe.
Excellent. This is one of the most critical prescribing safety rules in respiratory pharmacology — always pair a LABA with an ICS in asthma. Note that LABA monotherapy is acceptable in COPD.

interactions.label: A patient with allergic rhinitis complains primarily of severe nasal congestion

params.question: A patient with allergic rhinitis complains primarily of severe nasal congestion that has not improved with oral cetirizine. Which drug class would most effectively address all four nasal symptoms, including congestion?

answers.text: Oral second-generation antihistamines at a higher dose

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Antihistamines relieve sneezing, itching, and rhinorrhoea, but nasal congestion is driven mainly by alpha-adrenergic pathways rather than histamine. Increasing the dose will not overcome this mechanistic limitation.

answers.text: Topical nasal decongestants such as oxymetazoline

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Decongestants relieve congestion rapidly by constricting nasal blood vessels, but they must not be used beyond five days because of rebound congestion (rhinitis medicamentosa). They also do not address sneezing or itching.

answers.text: Intranasal corticosteroids

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Intranasal corticosteroids suppress the entire inflammatory cascade in the nasal mucosa, effectively addressing all four symptom domains — sneezing, itching, rhinorrhoea, and congestion — making them the most effective single drug class.

answers.text: Oral leukotriene receptor antagonists such as montelukast

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Montelukast has a modest effect on rhinitis symptoms and is less effective than intranasal corticosteroids as a single agent, particularly for congestion relief.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: histamine drives sneezing and itching, but congestion is mainly alpha-adrenergic. Only intranasal corticosteroids cover all four nasal symptom domains — sneezing, itching, rhinorrhoea, and congestion — effectively.

Spot on. Intranasal corticosteroids are the gold standard for allergic rhinitis because they act across all symptom domains, unlike antihistamines (which miss congestion) or decongestants (which risk rebound).

interactions.label: A patient with a lower respiratory tract infection presents with a productive co

params.question: A patient with a lower respiratory tract infection presents with a productive cough bringing up mucopurulent sputum. Which management approach is most appropriate?

answers.text: Prescribe codeine to suppress the cough and allow rest

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Codeine suppresses the cough reflex centrally, which would impair clearance of infected secretions and potentially worsen the underlying infection by allowing mucus to pool in the airways.

answers.text: Use dextromethorphan at bedtime to reduce nocturnal cough frequency

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Dextromethorphan is an antitussive appropriate only for dry, non-productive cough. In productive cough, suppressing the reflex hinders clearance of secretions the body needs to expel.

answers.text: Facilitate secretion clearance with expectorants, adequate hydration, and chest physiotherapy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. When cough is productive, the reflex is protective — it is doing useful work clearing mucus from the airways. The goal is to assist that clearance, not suppress it.

answers.text: Combine an antitussive with a mucolytic to suppress the cough while thinning secretions

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This combination is counterproductive: the mucolytic thins secretions for easier clearance, but the antitussive suppresses the very reflex needed to expel them.

overallFeedback.feedback: The cardinal rule: productive cough is protective. Suppressing it with antitussives impairs secretion clearance and can worsen the underlying condition. Facilitate, do not suppress.
Well done. The first question in cough management is always: is this cough doing useful work? If productive, facilitate clearance; never suppress.

interactions.label: A 52-year-old non-smoking woman on enalapril for hypertension develops a persist

params.question: A 52-year-old non-smoking woman on enalapril for hypertension develops a persistent dry cough lasting ten weeks. Her chest X-ray is normal. What is the most appropriate first step in management?

answers.text: Prescribe codeine linctus for symptomatic relief while investigating further

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Symptomatic suppression without addressing the likely cause is inappropriate here. ACE inhibitor-induced cough is one of the most common causes of chronic dry cough and resolves with drug substitution.

answers.text: Start intranasal corticosteroids for suspected post-nasal drip

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While post-nasal drip is a common cause of chronic cough, a patient on an ACE inhibitor who develops a dry cough must first have the medication addressed — it is the most likely and easily reversible cause.

answers.text: Switch enalapril to an angiotensin receptor blocker

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. ACE inhibitors cause dry cough by increasing bradykinin levels. The cough typically resolves within one to four weeks of switching to an ARB, which does not affect bradykinin metabolism.

answers.text: Order high-resolution CT of the chest to exclude interstitial lung disease

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: With a normal chest X-ray and a clear temporal association with an ACE inhibitor, advanced imaging is premature. The first step is to remove the most probable iatrogenic cause.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the algorithm: in a non-smoker with chronic cough (more than eight weeks) and a normal chest X-ray, consider ACE inhibitor use, post-nasal drip, GERD, and cough-variant asthma. Always treat the underlying cause first.
Excellent. In chronic cough with a normal chest X-ray, always ask: is the patient on an ACE inhibitor? This is one of the most common and easily reversible drug-induced causes of cough.
